title.zh: 卷一百六十一 列傳第八十六 張趙李鄭徐王馮庾
title.en: Volume 161 Biographies 86: Zhang, Zhao, Li, Zheng, Xu, Wang, Feng, Yu
title.raw: 卷一百六十一 列傳第八十六 張趙李鄭徐王馮庾 Volume 161 Biographies 86: Zhang, Zhao, Li, Zheng, Xu, Wang, Feng, Yu

sentences.zh: 張趙李鄭徐王馮庾

translations.literal: Zhang, Zhao, Li, Zheng, Xu, Wang, Feng, Yu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, Zhao, Li, Zheng, Xu, Wang, Feng, and Yu

sentences.zh: 張薦，字孝舉，深州陸澤人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian, style name Xiaoju, was a man of Luze in Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian, whose style name was Xiaoju, came from Luze in Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖鷟，字文成，早惠絕倫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhuo, style name Wencheng, was precociously gifted beyond all peers.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhang Zhuo, styled Wencheng, showed precocious brilliance unmatched among his peers.

sentences.zh: 為兒時，夢紫文大鳥，五色成文，止其廷。

translations.literal: As a child, he dreamed of a great bird with purple markings, its plumage patterned in five colors, alighting in his courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood he dreamed of a great bird marked in purple, its feathers woven in five colors, that came to rest in his courtyard.

sentences.zh: 大父曰：「吾聞五色赤文，鳳也；

translations.literal: His grandfather said: "I have heard that five-colored plumage with red markings is the phoenix;
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather said, "I have heard that five-colored plumage with red markings is the phoenix;

sentences.zh: 紫文，鸑鷟也。

translations.literal: purple markings denote the zhuo bird.
translations.idiomatic: purple markings belong to the zhuo bird.

sentences.zh: 若壯，殆以文章瑞朝廷乎？」

translations.literal: When you grow up, will you perhaps bring literary glory to the court as an auspicious sign?"
translations.idiomatic: When you are grown, will you perhaps bring literary glory to the court as an auspicious sign?

sentences.zh: 遂命以名。

translations.literal: He thereupon gave him his name.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon gave him the name Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 調露初，登進士第。

translations.literal: In the early Tiaolu era, he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tiaolu reign, he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 考功員外郎騫味道見所對，稱天下無雙。

translations.literal: Wei Chawei, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, seeing his examination answers, declared him unmatched under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chawei of the Ministry of Personnel, on reading his examination answers, declared that no one under heaven could match him.

sentences.zh: 授岐王府參軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed adjutant in the household of the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed adjutant in the household of the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 八以制舉皆甲科，再調長安尉，遷鴻臚丞。

translations.literal: Eight times he took the decree examination, each time with top honors; twice appointed as assistant magistrate of Chang'an, then promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Eight times he entered the decree examination and each time took top honors; twice he was posted as assistant magistrate of Chang'an, then promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 四參選，判策為銓府最。

translations.literal: On his fourth presentation for office, his policy essays ranked highest in the Board of Appointment.
translations.idiomatic: On his fourth presentation for appointment, his policy essays ranked first in the Board of Appointment.

sentences.zh: 員外郎員半千數為公卿稱「鷟文辭猶青銅錢，萬選萬中」，時號鷟「青錢學士」。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Yuan Banqian repeatedly praised him before the princes and ministers, saying "Zhuo's literary compositions are like bronze cash—ten thousand selections, ten thousand hits"; he was called the "Bronze Cash Scholar."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Yuan Banqian often told the princes and ministers that Zhuo's prose was like bronze cash—ten thousand choices, ten thousand hits—and the age called Zhuo the Bronze Cash Scholar.

sentences.zh: 證聖中，天官侍郎劉奇以鷟及司馬锽為御史。

translations.literal: During the Zhensheng reign, Vice Director of the Bureau of Astronomy Liu Qi recommended Zhuo and Sima Zheng as censors.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhensheng era, vice director of the Bureau of Astronomy Liu Qi recommended Zhuo and Sima Zheng for appointment as censors.

sentences.zh: 性躁卞，儻蕩無檢，罕為正人所遇，姚崇尤惡之。

translations.literal: His nature was impetuous and blunt; he was unrestrained and without decorum, rarely meeting with approval from upright men, and Yao Chong especially hated him.
translations.idiomatic: He was impetuous and blunt by nature, unrestrained and without decorum, seldom met with favor from upright men, and Yao Chong especially detested him.

sentences.zh: 開元初，御史李全交劾鷟多口語訕短時政，貶嶺南；

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era, Censor Li Quanjiao impeached Zhuo for repeatedly speaking in mockery and denigration of current affairs; he was demoted to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, censor Li Quanjiao impeached Zhuo for repeatedly mocking and denigrating current affairs, and he was demoted to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書李日知訟斥太重，得內徙。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Li Rizhi protested that the punishment was too severe; he was permitted an internal transfer instead.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Li Rizhi protested that the sentence was too harsh, and Zhuo was allowed an internal transfer instead.

sentences.zh: 鷟屬文下筆輒成，浮艷少理致，其論著率詆誚蕪猥，然大行一時，晚進莫不傳記。

translations.literal: Zhuo's literary compositions flowed from his brush as soon as he set pen to paper, but they were florid and shallow in intellectual substance; his essays mostly traded in ridicule and vulgarity, yet they were widely circulated for a time, and younger scholars all copied and transmitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's compositions came from his brush at once, but they were florid and thin in substance; his essays mostly traded in ridicule and vulgarity, yet for a time they circulated everywhere, and younger scholars all copied and passed them on.

sentences.zh: 武後時，中人馬仙童陷默啜，問：「文成在否？」

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's reign, the eunuch Ma Xiantong was captured by Mohechuo, who asked: "Is Wencheng still alive?
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's reign, the eunuch Ma Xiantong was captured by Mohechuo, who asked, "Is Wencheng still alive?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「近自御史貶官。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Recently demoted from his post as censor."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "He was recently demoted from his post as censor."

sentences.zh: 曰：「國有此人不用，無能為也。」

translations.literal: Mohechuo said: "A state that has such a man and does not employ him cannot accomplish anything."
translations.idiomatic: Mohechuo said, "A state that has such a man and does not use him cannot accomplish anything."

sentences.zh: 新羅、日本使至，必出金寶購其文。

translations.literal: When envoys from Silla and Japan arrived, they invariably brought gold and treasures to purchase his writings.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys from Silla and Japan arrived, they always brought gold and treasures to buy his writings.

sentences.zh: 終司門員外郎。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Vice Director of the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as vice director of the Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 薦敏銳有文辭，能為《周官》、《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: Jian was quick-witted and skilled in literary composition; he could lecture on the Rites of Zhou and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was quick-witted and gifted in letters; he could expound the Rites of Zhou and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 初，為顏真卿嘆賞。

translations.literal: Early on, he won the admiration of Yan Zhenqing.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he won Yan Zhenqing's admiration.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，浙西觀察使李涵表薦才任史官，詔授左司禦率府兵曹參軍，以母老辭不就。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, Zhexi Observation Commissioner Li Han memorialized recommending Jian as qualified for the office of historiographer; an edict appointed him Left Assistant in the Imperial Guard Bureau's Military Affairs section, but he declined on grounds that his mother was elderly.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era, Zhexi observation commissioner Li Han memorialized that Jian was fit to serve as historiographer; an edict appointed him military affairs assistant in the Imperial Guard Bureau, but he declined because his mother was old.

sentences.zh: 喪除，禮部侍郎於邵以聞，召充史館修撰，兼陽翟尉。

translations.literal: After the mourning period ended, Vice Minister of Rites Yu Shao reported this to the throne; he was summoned to serve as reviser in the Historiography Institute, concurrently as assistant magistrate of Yangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, vice minister of rites Yu Shao reported this to the throne, and Jian was summoned to serve as reviser in the Historiography Institute while also holding the post of assistant magistrate of Yangzhai.

sentences.zh: 真卿為李希烈所拘，遣兄子峴及家仆奏事，五輩皆留內客省，不得出。

translations.literal: Zhenqing, held captive by Li Xilie, sent his elder brother's son Xian and household servants to present memorials; five delegations in all were detained at the Internal Guests Office and could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing, held captive by Li Xilie, sent his elder brother's son Xian and household servants to present memorials; all five delegations were detained at the Internal Guests Office and could not leave.

sentences.zh: 薦上疏曰：

translations.literal: Jian submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: Jian submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 去正月中，真卿奉使淮西，期不先戒，行無素備。

translations.literal: Last first month, Zhenqing went on mission to Huaixi without prior warning, his journey made without usual preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Last first month, Zhenqing went on mission to Huaixi without prior warning and set out without his usual preparations.

sentences.zh: 受命之後，不宿於家，親黨不遑告別，介副不及陳請，孱僮單騎，即日載馳。

translations.literal: After receiving his commission, he did not lodge at home; relatives had no time to be informed; aides had no chance to petition; with a feeble servant and a single horse, he set out the same day.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving his commission he did not stay the night at home; relatives had no time for farewells; aides had no chance to petition; with a frail servant and a single horse he set out the same day.

sentences.zh: 冒奸鋒於臨汝，折元惡於許下，捐軀杖義，威詬群兇，遂令脅制者回慮，忠勇者肆情。

translations.literal: He braved the rebels' vanguard at Ruyu and broke the chief culprit at Xuzhou, risking his body and upholding righteousness, his authority rebuking the mass of villains, causing those under coercion to reconsider and the loyal and brave to act freely.
translations.idiomatic: He braved the rebels' vanguard at Ruyu and broke the chief culprit at Xuzhou, risking his body in the service of righteousness and rebuking the mass of villains, so that those under coercion reconsidered and the loyal and brave acted freely.

sentences.zh: 周曾奮發於外，韋清伺應於內，希烈蒼黃窘迫，奔固舊穴，蓋真卿義風所激也。

translations.literal: Zhou Zeng roused himself from without, Wei Qing watched for opportunity within; Xilie, flustered and hard pressed, fled to fortify his old lair—largely stirred by Zhenqing's righteous spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zeng roused himself from without and Wei Qing watched for opportunity within; Xilie, flustered and hard pressed, fled to fortify his old lair—largely stirred by Zhenqing's righteous example.

sentences.zh: 真卿逮事四朝，為國元老，忠直孝友，羽儀王室。

translations.literal: Zhenqing served four reigns as a senior statesman of the realm, loyal, upright, filial, and friendly—a model ornament to the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing had served four reigns as a senior statesman of the realm, loyal, upright, filial, and friendly—a model ornament to the royal house.

sentences.zh: 行年八十，被羸老之疾，拘囚環堵之間，顧眄鉤戟之下，呼嗟憤恚，失寢忘食，不知悲翁何以堪此！

translations.literal: At eighty years of age, afflicted with the infirmities of age, imprisoned between four walls, looking up at hooked halberds above him, sighing in rage and indignation, losing sleep and forgetting to eat—who knows how an aged man in sorrow could endure this!
translations.idiomatic: At eighty, afflicted with the infirmities of age, imprisoned between four walls and looking up at hooked halberds above him, sighing in rage and indignation, losing sleep and forgetting to eat—who knows how an aged man in sorrow could endure this!

sentences.zh: 伏聞希烈之母，鐘念幼子，目不絕泣，求責希烈；

translations.literal: I have heard that Xilie's mother, cherishing her young son, never ceased weeping, demanding that Xilie be held accountable;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Xilie's mother, cherishing her young son, never ceased weeping and demanded that Xilie be held accountable;

sentences.zh: 又希烈妻祖母郭及妻妹封並逮捕京師。

translations.literal: also that Xilie's wife, grandmother Guo, and wife's sister Feng were all arrested and brought to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: also that Xilie's wife, his grandmother Guo, and his wife's sister Feng were all arrested and brought to the capital.

sentences.zh: 此三人留之無益，請寘境上以贖真卿，先降詔書，分明諭告。

translations.literal: Keeping these three persons gains nothing; please place them on the border to ransom Zhenqing, first issuing an edict clearly announcing this policy.
translations.idiomatic: Keeping these three persons gains nothing; please place them on the border to ransom Zhenqing, first issuing an edict that clearly announces this policy.

sentences.zh: 且希烈知真卿人望，不敢加害，既無嫌隙，但因循未遣耳。

translations.literal: Moreover Xilie knows Zhenqing's standing among men and dares not harm him; there is no grudge between them, but he has simply procrastinated in not sending him back.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Xilie knows Zhenqing's standing among men and dares not harm him; there is no grudge between them, but he has simply procrastinated in not sending him back.

sentences.zh: 若歸其親愛，賊亦何吝還一使哉？

translations.literal: If their loved ones are returned, would the rebel begrudge returning one envoy?
translations.idiomatic: If their loved ones are returned, would the rebel begrudge returning one envoy?

sentences.zh: 臣又聞真卿所遣兄子峴及家僮從官奉表來者五輩，皆留中，其子頵等拳拳實希一見，望許休澣，告以安否。

translations.literal: I have also heard that Xian, the nephew Zhenqing sent, and household servants and attending officials who came bearing memorials—five delegations in all—are all held within the palace; his son Yun and others earnestly hope for a single audience; I beg permission for them to rest on their leave days and be told whether he is safe.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that Xian, the nephew Zhenqing sent, and the household servants and attending officials who came bearing memorials—five delegations in all—are all held within the palace; his son Yun and others earnestly hope for a single audience; I beg that they be allowed leave days and told whether he is safe.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，盧杞持之，不報。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Lu Qi held it back and no reply was issued.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Lu Qi held it back and no reply was issued.

sentences.zh: 朱泚反，詭姓名伏匿城中，著《史遁先生傳》。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he took a false name and hid concealed in the city, composing "Biography of Master Shitun."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he took a false name and hid in the city, composing the Biography of Master Shitun.

sentences.zh: 京師平，擢左拾遺。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, he was promoted to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was pacified, he was promoted to left reminder.

sentences.zh: 詔復用杞為刺史，薦與陳京、趙需等論杞奸惡傾覆不當用，入對挺確，德宗納之。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to reinstate Qi as prefect; Jian, together with Chen Jing, Zhao Xu, and others, argued that Qi's wickedness and overturning of the realm made him unfit for appointment; appearing before the throne he spoke firmly, and Dezong accepted their view.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued to reinstate Qi as prefect; Jian, together with Chen Jing, Zhao Xu, and others, argued that Qi's wickedness and his overturning of the realm made him unfit for appointment; appearing before the throne he spoke firmly, and Dezong accepted their view.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，帝親郊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, the emperor personally performed the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyuan, the emperor personally performed the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 時更兵亂，禮物殘替，用薦為太常博士，參綴典儀，略如舊章。

translations.literal: At that time, after successive military upheavals, ritual implements were damaged and missing; Jian was appointed Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to assist in arranging the ceremonial statutes, approximating the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, after successive military upheavals, ritual implements were damaged and missing; Jian was appointed doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to assist in arranging the ceremonial statutes, approximating the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書關播持節送鹹安公主於回紇，以薦為判官。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Guan Bo, holding credentials to escort Princess Xian'an to the Uyghurs, took Jian as his executive officer.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Guan Bo, bearing credentials to escort Princess Xian'an to the Uyghurs, took Jian as his executive officer.

sentences.zh: 還，遷工部員外郎。

translations.literal: On return, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢諫議大夫，復為史館修撰。

translations.literal: After some time, he was promoted to Remonstrating Censor and again served as reviser in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to remonstrating censor and again served as reviser in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 方裴延齡用事，中傷俊良，建白無不當帝意。

translations.literal: At that time Pei Yanling was in power, slandering worthy men; whatever proposals he made invariably suited the emperor's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Yanling was in power, slandering worthy men; whatever proposals he made invariably suited the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 薦將疏其惡，延齡知之，因言於帝曰：「諫議論朝政得失，史官書人君善惡，二者不可兼。」

translations.literal: Jian was about to memorialize denouncing his wickedness; Yanling learned of it and therefore said to the emperor: "A remonstrating censor discusses the gains and losses of court governance, while the historiographer records the ruler's good and evil—one person cannot hold both offices.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was about to memorialize denouncing his wickedness; Yanling learned of it and therefore said to the emperor, "A remonstrating censor discusses the gains and losses of court governance, while the historiographer records the ruler's good and evil—one person cannot hold both offices.

sentences.zh: 薦改秘書少監。

translations.literal: Jian was changed to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 延齡必欲以罪斥廢之。

translations.literal: Yanling was determined to find some offense by which to dismiss and banish him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling was determined to find some offense by which to dismiss and banish him.

sentences.zh: 會遣使冊回鶻毗伽懷信可汗，使薦至回鶻。

translations.literal: When an envoy was sent to invest Bilge Huai Trust Khan of the Uyghurs, Yanling had Jian sent to the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: When an envoy was sent to invest Bilge Huai Trust Khan of the Uyghurs, Yanling had Jian sent to the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 還為監。

translations.literal: On return he served as director.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he served as director of the Directorate of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃贊普死，擢薦工部侍郎，為吊祭使。

translations.literal: When the Tibetan king died, Jian was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and made condolence envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetan king died, Jian was promoted to vice minister of works and made condolence envoy.

sentences.zh: 薦占對詳辯，三使絕域，始兼侍御史、中丞，後大夫。

translations.literal: Jian's responses in audience were detailed and eloquent; on three missions to distant regions he began as concurrent attendant censor and then vice censor-in-chief, later chief censor.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's responses in audience were detailed and eloquent; on three missions to distant regions he began as concurrent attendant censor and then vice censor-in-chief, and later served as chief censor.

sentences.zh: 次赤嶺，被病卒，年六十一，吐蕃傳其柩以歸。

translations.literal: At Chiling he fell ill and died, aged sixty-one; the Tibetans conveyed his coffin on the return journey.
translations.idiomatic: At Chiling he fell ill and died, aged sixty-one; the Tibetans conveyed his coffin on the return journey.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，問至，贈禮部尚書，謚曰憲。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong acceded, he inquired after Jian; he was posthumously granted Minister of Rites with the posthumous name Xian (Diligent).
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong acceded, he inquired after Jian; he was posthumously granted minister of rites with the posthumous name Xian.

sentences.zh: 薦自拾遺至侍郎，凡二十年，常兼史館修撰。

translations.literal: From Reminder to Vice Minister, over twenty years in all, Jian constantly also served as reviser in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: From reminder to vice minister, over twenty years in all, Jian constantly also served as reviser in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 初，貞元時，京師旱，帝避正殿，減膳，薦白限日以應古制。

translations.literal: Early in the Zhenyuan era, when the capital suffered drought, the emperor left the main hall and reduced his meals; Jian memorialized setting a time limit according to ancient practice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan era, when the capital suffered drought, the emperor left the main hall and reduced his meals; Jian memorialized setting a time limit according to ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 及定昭德皇后廟樂，遷獻、懿二祖，定太儀位號、大臣祔廟鼓吹法，莫不參裁，諸儒謂博而詳。

translations.literal: When determining the music for Empress Zhaode's temple, moving the two ancestors Xian and Yi, fixing Empress Taiyi's title, regulations for enshrining great ministers and for funeral dirges and processional music—all were deliberated with his participation; the classicists called his knowledge broad and detailed.
translations.idiomatic: When determining the music for Empress Zhaode's temple, moving the two ancestors Xian and Yi, fixing Empress Taiyi's title, and regulations for enshrining great ministers and for funeral dirges and processional music—all were deliberated with his participation; the classicists called his knowledge broad and detailed.

sentences.zh: 所著書百餘篇。

translations.literal: His written works numbered over a hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His written works numbered more than a hundred pieces.

sentences.zh: 子又新，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Youxin has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Youxin has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 孫讀，字聖用，幼穎解。

translations.literal: His grandson Du, style name Shengyong, was precociously intelligent as a child.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zhang Du, styled Shengyong, was precociously intelligent as a child.

sentences.zh: 大中時第進士，鄭薰辟署宣州幕府。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era he passed the jinshi, and Zheng Xun recruited him to his staff in the Xuanzhou prefectural headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong era he passed the jinshi examination, and Zheng Xun recruited him to his staff at the Xuanzhou prefectural headquarters.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose through the ranks to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 中和初為吏部，選牒精允。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhonghe era he served in the Ministry of Personnel; his selection registers were meticulous and fair.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhonghe era he served in the Ministry of Personnel; his selection registers were meticulous and fair.

sentences.zh: 調官丐留二年，詔可，榜其事曹門。

translations.literal: He begged to remain in office two more years; the edict approved, and his deed was posted at the gate of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to remain in office two more years; the edict approved, and his deed was posted at the gate of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 後兼弘文館學士，判院事，卒。

translations.literal: Later he also served as scholar of the Hongwen Academy and managed its affairs; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also served as scholar of the Hongwen Academy and managed its affairs; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 趙涓，冀州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Juan, a native of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Juan was a native of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼有文，天寶時第進士，補郾城尉，稍歷臺省。

translations.literal: Gifted with letters from youth, he passed the jinshi in the Tianbao era, was appointed assistant magistrate of Yancheng, and gradually served in the central secretariat and ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted with letters from youth, he passed the jinshi in the Tianbao era, was appointed assistant magistrate of Yancheng, and gradually served in the central secretariat and ministries.

sentences.zh: 河南王縉引署副元帥府判官。

translations.literal: Henan Governor Wang Jin recruited him as executive officer on the deputy commander's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Henan governor Wang Jin recruited him as executive officer on the deputy commander's staff.

sentences.zh: 德宗初，為衢州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dezong's reign he served as prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dezong's reign he served as prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 始，永泰時，禁中火，近東宮，代宗疑之。

translations.literal: Originally, in the Yongtai era, a fire broke out in the forbidden palace near the Eastern Palace; Daizong harbored suspicions.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, in the Yongtai era, a fire broke out in the forbidden palace near the Eastern Palace, and Daizong harbored suspicions.

sentences.zh: 涓以監察御史為巡使，驗治明諦，跡火所來，乃宦人直舍。

translations.literal: Juan, as supervising censor, served as investigation commissioner; his inquiry was clear and precise, tracing the fire to eunuchs' quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Juan, as supervising censor, served as investigation commissioner; his inquiry was clear and precise, and he traced the fire to the eunuchs' quarters.

sentences.zh: 帝在東宮頗德之。

translations.literal: The emperor, then crown prince, was deeply grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, then crown prince, was deeply grateful to him.

sentences.zh: 及治衢，不為觀察使韓滉所容，奏免官。

translations.literal: When governing Qu, he was not tolerated by Observation Commissioner Han Huang, who memorialized for his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: When governing Quzhou, he was not tolerated by observation commissioner Han Huang, who memorialized for his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 帝見其名，問宰相曰：「是豈永泰時御史乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor saw his name and asked the chief minister: "Is this not the censor from the Yongtai era?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw his name and asked the chief minister, "Is this not the censor from the Yongtai era?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「然。」

translations.literal: He answered: "It is."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "It is."

sentences.zh: 詔拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 既至，勞之曰：「卿正直，朕所自知，乃以罪聞，不信也。」

translations.literal: When Juan arrived, the emperor comforted him, saying: "You are upright—I know this myself; to hear that you committed an offense—I do not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: When Juan arrived, the emperor comforted him, saying, "You are upright—I know this myself; to hear that you committed an offense—I do not believe it.

sentences.zh: 命典吏部選。

translations.literal: He was ordered to preside over personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to preside over personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 從狩梁。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor on the campaign to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor on the campaign to Liang.

sentences.zh: 興元元年卒，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Xingyuan; posthumously granted Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Xingyuan and was posthumously granted minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 子博宣，亦擢進士第。

translations.literal: His son Boxuan also passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Boxuan also passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 藻翰豪邁，沈於酒，傲忽少檢。

translations.literal: His literary compositions were bold and lofty; steeped in wine, arrogant and careless with little restraint.
translations.idiomatic: His literary compositions were bold and lofty; steeped in wine, he was arrogant and careless with little restraint.

sentences.zh: 陳許曲環辟署於府，久不能堪，乃誣「受吳少誠金為反間，數言休咎惑眾」。

translations.literal: Qu Huan of Chenxu recruited him to his headquarters; unable to endure it long, Huan falsely accused him of "receiving gold from Wu Shaochuan as a spy, repeatedly speaking of fortune and misfortune to delude the masses."
translations.idiomatic: Qu Huan of Chenxu recruited him to his headquarters; unable to endure him long, Huan falsely accused him of receiving gold from Wu Shaochuan as a spy and repeatedly speaking of fortune and misfortune to delude the masses.

sentences.zh: 有詔杖四十，流康州，時人冤之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered forty strokes of the rod and exile to Kangzhou; contemporaries considered this unjust.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered forty strokes of the rod and exile to Kangzhou; contemporaries considered this unjust.

sentences.zh: 李紓，字仲舒。

translations.literal: Li Shu, style name Zhongshu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shu, whose style name was Zhongshu.

sentences.zh: 始仕為校書郎，大歷初，李季卿薦為左補闕，遷累中書舍人。

translations.literal: He began his career as proofreader; in early Dali, Li Jiqing recommended him as Left Supplements Clerk; he rose through the ranks to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as proofreader; in early Dali, Li Jiqing recommended him as left supplements clerk, and he rose through the ranks to secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 德宗居奉天，繇禮部侍郎選為同州刺史。

translations.literal: When Dezong was at Fengtian, he was selected from Vice Minister of Rites to be prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong was at Fengtian, he was selected from vice minister of rites to be prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝次梁，紓委城趨行在，擢兵部侍郎、高邑伯。

translations.literal: When the emperor stopped at Liang, Shu abandoned his prefecture and hurried to the traveling court; he was promoted Vice Minister of War and created Baron of Gaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor stopped at Liang, Shu abandoned his prefecture and hurried to the traveling court; he was promoted vice minister of war and created baron of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 建言享武成王廟不宜與文宣王等，制從之。

translations.literal: He proposed that offerings at the temple of Martial King of Completion should not rank equal with Confucius; the regulation followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that offerings at the temple of the Martial King of Completion should not rank equal with Confucius; the regulation followed his view.

sentences.zh: 紓性樂易，喜接後進。

translations.literal: Shu's nature was easygoing; he delighted in receiving younger scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was easygoing by nature and delighted in receiving younger scholars.

sentences.zh: 其自奉養頗華裕，不為齪齪崖檢。

translations.literal: His own upkeep was quite luxurious and ample; he was not petty or rigid in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His own upkeep was quite luxurious and ample; he was not petty or rigid in conduct.

sentences.zh: 官雖貴，則遊縱自如。

translations.literal: Though his office was exalted, he roamed and indulged himself as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Though his office was exalted, he roamed and indulged himself as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 奉詔為《興元紀功述》及它郊廟樂章，論撰甚多。

translations.literal: By imperial order he composed "Account of Merits at Xingyuan" and other suburban and temple music texts; his writings were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he composed the Account of Merits at Xingyuan and other suburban and temple music texts; his writings were numerous.

sentences.zh: 進吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 年六十二卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died aged sixty-two; posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two and was posthumously granted minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 鄭雲達，系本滎陽。

translations.literal: Zheng Yunda, whose clan was originally from Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yunda came of a line originally from Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 父戶，為郾城尉，州刺史移職，民之暴謷者遮道留，戶誅殺六七人。

translations.literal: His father Hu served as assistant magistrate of Yancheng; when the prefect was transferred, unruly protestors blocked the road to detain him, and Hu killed six or seven men.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hu served as assistant magistrate of Yancheng; when the prefect was transferred, violent protesters blocked the road to detain him, and Hu killed six or seven of them.

sentences.zh: 采訪使奇之，言狀，擢北海尉。

translations.literal: The investigation commissioner was impressed and reported the facts; he was promoted to assistant magistrate of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: The investigation commissioner was impressed, reported what had happened, and Hu was promoted to assistant magistrate of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，縣民孫俊驅市人以應，戶率眾擊殺之。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, a county man named Sun Jun drove townspeople to respond; Hu led the crowd and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, a county man Sun Jun drove townspeople to respond; Hu led the people and killed him.

sentences.zh: 改登州司馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as military affairs officer of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military affairs officer of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 李光弼表為武寧府判官，遷沂州刺史，諭降賊李浩五千人。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi memorialized appointing him executive officer of the Wuning headquarters; he was transferred to prefect of Yizhou and persuaded five thousand rebels under Li Hao to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi memorialized him as executive officer of the Wuning headquarters; he was transferred to prefect of Yizhou and persuaded five thousand rebels under Li Hao to surrender.

sentences.zh: 終滁州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended his career as prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 雲達為人誕譎敢言，已登進士第，去客燕朔，朱泚善之，表為掌書記，妻以滔女。

translations.literal: Yunda was boastful and bold in speech; having passed the jinshi, he left to sojourn in Yan and Shuobei; Zhu Ci favored him, memorialized him as chief secretary, and gave him Zhu Tao's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yunda was boastful and bold in speech; having passed the jinshi, he went to sojourn in Yan and the northern frontier; Zhu Ci favored him, appointed him chief secretary by memorial, and gave him Zhu Tao's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 泚將朝，使雲達先入奏，同府蔡廷玉譖於泚，奏貶為平州參軍。

translations.literal: When Ci was about to attend court, he had Yunda enter first to present a memorial; Cai Tingyu of the same headquarters slandered him to Ci, and he was memorialized demoted to military adjutant of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Ci was about to attend court, he had Yunda enter first to present a memorial; Cai Tingyu of the same headquarters slandered him to Ci, and he was memorialized for demotion to military adjutant of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 滔代泚將，復辟雲達為判官。

translations.literal: When Tao replaced Ci as commander, he again recruited Yunda as executive officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao replaced Ci as commander, he again recruited Yunda as executive officer.

sentences.zh: 廷玉與要藉官朱體微它日與泚從容言：「滔非長者，不可付以兵。」

translations.literal: Tingyu and the palace attendant Zhu Tiwei once spoke to Ci at leisure: "Tao is not a man of mature character; troops must not be entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu and palace attendant Zhu Tiwei once spoke casually to Ci: "Tao is not a man of mature character; you must not entrust troops to him.

sentences.zh: 雲達數漏其語以怒滔，故滔論廷玉等，皆得罪死。

translations.literal: Yunda repeatedly leaked their words to anger Tao; therefore Tao accused Tingyu and the others, and all were condemned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yunda repeatedly leaked their words to anger Tao; therefore Tao impeached Tingyu and the others, and all were condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 滔助田悅，雲達諫，不從，遂棄室自歸。

translations.literal: When Tao aided Tian Yue, Yunda remonstrated; not obeyed, he abandoned his household and returned on his own.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao aided Tian Yue, Yunda remonstrated; when his advice went unheeded, he abandoned his household and returned on his own.

sentences.zh: 德宗悅，擢諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Dezong was pleased and promoted him to Remonstrating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was pleased and promoted him to remonstrating censor.

sentences.zh: 帝在梁，雲達依李晟，晟表以禮部侍郎為軍司馬，時時咨逮戎略。

translations.literal: When the emperor was at Liang, Yunda attached himself to Li Sheng; Sheng memorialized him as Vice Minister of Rites serving as army marshal, and frequently consulted him on military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at Liang, Yunda attached himself to Li Sheng; Sheng memorialized appointing him vice minister of rites as army marshal, and frequently consulted him on military strategy.

sentences.zh: 元和初，為京兆尹，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, he served as metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe he served as metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and died in office.

sentences.zh: 弟方達，悖悍，結徒剽劫，父欲殺之，不克。

translations.literal: His younger brother Fangda was perverse and fierce, gathering followers to plunder and rob; the father wished to kill him but could not.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Fangda was violent and fierce, gathering followers to plunder and rob; their father wished to kill him but could not.

sentences.zh: 雲達自劾「不能教，恐赤臣家」。

translations.literal: Yunda impeached himself: "Unable to teach him, I fear I will bring shame upon my clan."
translations.idiomatic: Yunda impeached himself, saying, "Unable to teach him, I fear I will bring shame upon our household."

sentences.zh: 詔錮死黔州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him imprisoned until death in Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Fangda imprisoned until death in Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 徐岱，字處仁，蘇州嘉興人，世農家子。

translations.literal: Xu Dai, style name Churen, was a native of Jiaxing in Suzhou, from a farming family for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Dai, styled Churen, came from Jiaxing in Suzhou; his family had been farmers for generations.

sentences.zh: 於學無所不通，辯論明銳，座人常屈。

translations.literal: In learning there was nothing he did not master; in debate he was sharp and clear, and those seated with him often yielded.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered every branch of learning; in debate he was sharp and clear, and those who sat with him often yielded.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，劉晏表為校書郎。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, Liu Yan memorialized him as collator.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era Liu Yan memorialized him as collator.

sentences.zh: 觀察使李棲筠欽其賢，署所居為「復禮鄉」。

translations.literal: Observation Commissioner Li Qiyun admired his virtue and designated his residence district as "Fuli Township" (Return to Rites).
translations.idiomatic: Observation commissioner Li Qiyun admired his virtue and designated the place where he lived as "Fuli Township."

sentences.zh: 名達於朝，擢偃師尉。

translations.literal: His fame reached the court; he was promoted to assistant magistrate of Yanshi.
translations.idiomatic: His fame reached the court and he was promoted to assistant magistrate of Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使蔣鎮薦為太常博士，專掌禮事。

translations.literal: Ritual Commissioner Jiang Zhen recommended him as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, exclusively overseeing ritual affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual commissioner Jiang Zhen recommended him as doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, put in charge of ritual affairs.

sentences.zh: 從德宗出奉天，以膳部員外郎兼博士。

translations.literal: He followed Dezong to Fengtian and served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Court Revenues, concurrently as doctor.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Dezong to Fengtian and served as vice director of the Ministry of Court Revenues while also holding the doctorate.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，為太子、諸王侍讀，遷給事中、史館修撰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan, he served as lecturer to the crown prince and princes; he was transferred to Attendant in the Palace Secretariat and reviser in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan he lectured to the crown prince and the imperial princes, then was transferred to attendant in the Palace Secretariat and reviser in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 帝以誕日歲歲詔佛老者大論麟德殿，並召岱及趙需、許孟容、韋渠牟講說。

translations.literal: On his birthday each year the emperor ordered great debates between Buddhists and Daoists in Linde Hall, summoning Dai together with Zhao Xu, Xu Mengrong, and Wei Qumou to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: Each year on his birthday the emperor ordered great debates between Buddhists and Daoists in Linde Hall, and summoned Dai together with Zhao Xu, Xu Mengrong, and Wei Qumou to expound.

sentences.zh: 始三家若矛楯然，卒而同歸於善。

translations.literal: At first the three schools were like spear and shield, but in the end all returned to the good.
translations.idiomatic: At first the three schools clashed like spear against shield, but in the end all returned to the good.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賚予有差。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed rewards in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed rewards in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 兩宮恩遇無比。

translations.literal: Favor from both palace and empress dowager was unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Favor from both the inner and outer palaces was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 性篤慎，至宮殿中語未嘗近之，不談人短，宗族孤孺者皆為婚嫁。

translations.literal: His nature was sincere and cautious; even within the palace he never spoke inappropriately, did not discuss others' faults, and arranged marriages for orphaned kin of the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Sincere and cautious by nature, he never used familiar language even within the palace, did not discuss others' faults, and arranged marriages for orphaned and widowed kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 然吝嗇，自持家管鑰，世所譏雲。

translations.literal: Yet he was stingy, keeping the household keys himself—a thing the age mocked.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was stingy and kept the household keys himself, which the age mocked.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 王仲舒，字弘中，并州祁人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongshu, style name Hongzhong, was a native of Qi in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongshu, styled Hongzhong, came from Qi in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少客江南，與梁肅、楊憑遊，有文稱。

translations.literal: In youth he sojourned in Jiangnan, traveled with Liang Su and Yang Ping, and enjoyed a literary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he sojourned in the south, kept company with Liang Su and Yang Ping, and gained a literary reputation.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，賢良方正高第，拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era he took top honors in the Worthy and Upright examination and was appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyuan he took top honors in the Worthy and Upright examination and was appointed left reminder.

sentences.zh: 德宗欲相裴延齡，與陽城交章言不可。

translations.literal: When Dezong wished to make Pei Yanling chief minister, he and Yang Cheng submitted linked memorials saying it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong wished to make Pei Yanling chief minister, he and Yang Cheng submitted linked memorials opposing it.

sentences.zh: 後入閣，帝顧宰相指曰：「是豈王仲舒邪？」

translations.literal: Later when entering the privy council, the emperor looked at the chief minister and pointed, saying: "Is that not Wang Zhongshu?
translations.idiomatic: Later when he entered the privy council, the emperor looked at the chief minister and pointed, saying, "Is that not Wang Zhongshu?

sentences.zh: 俄改右補闕，遷禮部考功員外郎。

translations.literal: Shortly he was changed to Right Supplements Clerk and transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites for Examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made right supplements clerk and transferred to vice director for examinations in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 奏議詳雅，省中伏其能。

translations.literal: His memorials were detailed and elegant; within the ministry all deferred to his ability.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials were detailed and elegant, and within the ministry all deferred to his ability.

sentences.zh: 坐累為連州司戶參軍，再徙荊南節度參謀。

translations.literal: Through accumulated fault he became census adjutant of Lianzhou, then was transferred again to staff officer on the Jingnan military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Through accumulated offenses he became census adjutant of Lianzhou, then was transferred again to staff officer on the Jingnan military commission.

sentences.zh: 元和初，召為吏部員外郎，未幾，知制誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, he was summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel; before long he was put in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel; before long he was put in charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 楊憑得罪斥去，無敢過其家，仲舒屢存之。

translations.literal: When Yang Ping was punished and expelled, no one dared visit his household; Zhongshu repeatedly called on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Ping was punished and expelled, no one dared visit his home; Zhongshu repeatedly called on him.

sentences.zh: 將直憑冤，貶峽州刺史，母喪解。

translations.literal: About to vindicate Ping's wrong, he was demoted to prefect of Xiazhou; maternal mourning released him from office.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to vindicate Ping's wrong, he was demoted to prefect of Xiazhou; he left office for maternal mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，為婺州刺史。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, he served as prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he served as prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 州疫旱，人徙死幾空；

translations.literal: The prefecture suffered plague and drought; people fled and died until it was nearly empty.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture suffered plague and drought; people fled and died until it was nearly empty.

sentences.zh: 居五年，裏閭增完，就加金紫服。

translations.literal: After five years in office, villages increased and were restored; he was promoted to wear gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: After five years villages were restored and flourishing, and he was given the gold-and-purple insignia of rank.

sentences.zh: 徙蘇州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 堤松江為路，變屋瓦，絕火災，賦調嘗與民為期，不擾自辦。

translations.literal: He diked the Song River as a roadway, changed roof tiles, eliminated conflagrations; tax levies he set deadlines with the people, who met them without disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: He diked the Song River to make a roadway, required tile roofs, eliminated major fires, and set tax deadlines with the people, who met them without disturbance.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，每言仲舒之文可思，最宜為誥，有古風。

translations.literal: When Muzong acceded, he often said Zhongshu's writings were worth pondering, most fit for edicts, and had an antique style.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong acceded, he often said Zhongshu's writings were worth pondering, most fit for edicts, and had an antique flavor.

sentences.zh: 召為中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 既至，視同列率新進少年，居不樂，曰：「豈可復治筆研於其間哉！

translations.literal: When he arrived, he saw his colleagues were mostly newly risen youths and was unhappy in the post, saying: "How could I again grind ink among them!
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, he saw his colleagues were mostly newly risen young men and was unhappy, saying, "How could I again grind ink among them!

sentences.zh: 吾久棄外，周知俗病利，得治之，不自愧。」

translations.literal: I have long been cast outside and know thoroughly the ills and profits of common practice; governing would not shame me.
translations.idiomatic: I have long been cast outside and know thoroughly the people's ills and profits; to govern them would not shame me.

sentences.zh: 宰相聞之，除江西觀察使。

translations.literal: When the chief minister heard this, he was appointed Jiangxi Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief minister heard this, he was appointed Jiangxi observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 初，江西榷酒利多佗州十八，民私釀，歲抵死不絕，谷數斛易鬥酒。

translations.literal: Originally Jiangxi's wine monopoly profit exceeded other prefectures by eighteenfold; the people brewed in secret, year after year suffering death penalties without end; several hu of grain traded for a dipper of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Jiangxi's wine-monopoly profit exceeded other prefectures by eighteen times; the people brewed in secret, and year after year those condemned to death did not cease; a few hu of grain bought a dipper of wine.

sentences.zh: 仲舒罷酤錢九十萬。

translations.literal: Zhongshu abolished ninety thousand strings of monopoly wine revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu abolished ninety thousand strings of monopoly wine revenue.

sentences.zh: 吏坐失官息錢五十萬，悉產不能償，仲舒焚簿書，脫械不問。

translations.literal: Officials were liable for fifty thousand strings of lost office interest, unable to repay from all their property; Zhongshu burned the ledgers, removed their shackles, and did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were liable for fifty thousand strings of lost office interest and could not repay from all their property; Zhongshu burned the ledgers, removed their shackles, and did not pursue the matter.

sentences.zh: 水旱，民賦不入，嘆曰：「我當減燕樂他用可乎！」

translations.literal: During flood and drought the people's taxes did not come in; he sighed: "Shall I reduce banquet music and use it for other purposes?
translations.idiomatic: During flood and drought the people's taxes did not come in; he sighed, "Shall I reduce banquet music and use the funds for other purposes?

sentences.zh: 為出錢二千萬代之。

translations.literal: He paid out twenty million cash to cover it on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: He paid out twenty million cash to cover it on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 有為佛老法、興浮屠祠屋者，皆驅出境。

translations.literal: Those who propagated Buddhist and Daoist teachings and built pagoda temples were all driven beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: Those who propagated Buddhist and Daoist teachings and built pagoda temples were all driven beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，年六十二，贈左散騎常侍，謚曰成。

translations.literal: He died in office, aged sixty-two; posthumously granted Left Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat with posthumous name Cheng (Accomplished).
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at sixty-two; he was posthumously granted left regular attendant at the Imperial Secretariat with the posthumous name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 仲舒尚義概，所居急民廢置，自為科條，初若煩密，久皆稱其便。

translations.literal: Zhongshu valued righteous boldness; wherever he governed he hastened to repair what the people had abandoned, drawing up regulations himself that at first seemed tedious but in time all called convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu valued righteous boldness; wherever he governed he hastened to repair what the people had abandoned; the regulations he drew up at first seemed tedious, but in time all praised their convenience.

sentences.zh: 馮伉，魏州元城人，徙貫京兆。

translations.literal: Feng Kang, a native of Yuancheng in Weizhou, later registered in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Kang came from Yuancheng in Weizhou and later registered his household in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 第五經、宏辭，調長安尉。

translations.literal: He passed the fifth classics examination and the Hongci examination; appointed assistant magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the fifth classics and Hongci examinations and was appointed assistant magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 三遷膳部員外郎，為睦王等侍讀。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Vice Director of the Ministry of Court Revenues and lecturer to the Prince of Mu and others.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became vice director of the Ministry of Court Revenues and lecturer to the Prince of Mu and others.

sentences.zh: 李抱真卒，伉持節臨吊，歸之帛，不受，又致京師，伉上表固拒。

translations.literal: When Li Baozhen died, Kang went with credentials to offer condolences; the returned silks he would not accept, and when they were sent again to the capital he memorialized firmly refusing.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Baozhen died, Kang went with credentials to offer condolences; he refused the returned silks, and when they were sent again to the capital he memorialized firmly refusing them.

sentences.zh: 於是醴泉令缺，宰相高選，德宗曰：「前使澤潞不受幣者，其人清，可用也。」

translations.literal: Then the magistrate of Liquan was vacant; the chief ministers made a careful selection; Dezong said: "The man who on the former mission to Ze-Lu would not accept gifts—that man is pure and can be used.
translations.idiomatic: Then the magistracy of Liquan fell vacant; the chief ministers made a careful selection; Dezong said, "The man who on the former mission to Ze-Lu would not accept gifts—that man is upright and can be used.

sentences.zh: 遂以授伉。

translations.literal: He was thereupon given the post to Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon given the post to Kang.

sentences.zh: 縣多嚚猾，數犯法，伉為著《諭蒙書》十四篇，大抵勸之務農、進學而教以忠孝。

translations.literal: The county had many unruly and cunning men who repeatedly broke the law; Kang composed fourteen chapters of "Instructions for the Untaught," mostly urging them to devote themselves to farming and advance in learning while teaching loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: The county had many unruly and cunning men who repeatedly broke the law; Kang composed fourteen chapters of Instructions for the Untaught, mostly urging farming and study while teaching loyalty and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 鄉鄉授之，使轉相教督。

translations.literal: Township by township he had them taught, causing them to instruct and supervise one another.
translations.idiomatic: Township by township he had them taught so they would instruct and supervise one another.

sentences.zh: 居七年，韋渠牟薦為給事中、皇太子諸王侍讀。

translations.literal: After seven years Wei Qumou recommended him as Attendant in the Palace Secretariat and lecturer to the crown prince and imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years Wei Qumou recommended him as attendant in the Palace Secretariat and lecturer to the crown prince and the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 對殿中，賜金紫服。

translations.literal: Appearing in audience in the hall, he was granted gold and purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: Appearing in audience in the hall, he was granted gold and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 進兵部侍郎，出為同州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted Vice Minister of War and sent out as prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted vice minister of war and sent out as prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 以散騎常侍召，領國子祭酒者再。

translations.literal: Summoned as Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat, he twice headed the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as regular attendant at the Imperial Secretariat, he twice served as director of education.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-six; posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-six and was posthumously granted minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 庾敬休，字順之，鄧州新野人。

translations.literal: Yu Jingxiu, style name Shunzhi, was a native of Xinye in Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jingxiu, styled Shunzhi, came from Xinye in Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖光烈，與弟光先不受安祿山偽官，遁去。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guanglie and his younger brother Guangxian refused offices under An Lushan's rebel regime and fled.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guanglie and Guangxian his younger brother refused offices under An Lushan's rebel regime and fled.

sentences.zh: 光烈終大理少卿，光先吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Guanglie died as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review; Guangxian as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Guanglie ended as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review; Guangxian as vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 父何，當朱泚反，又與弟倬逃山谷，不臣賊。

translations.literal: His father He, when Zhu Ci rebelled, again fled with his brother Zhuo into the mountains and would not serve the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: His father He, when Zhu Ci rebelled, again fled with his brother Zhuo into the mountains and would not serve the rebels.

sentences.zh: 官兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He ended as Director of the Bureau of Military Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as director of the Bureau of Military Appointments.

sentences.zh: 敬休擢進士第，又中宏辭，辟宣州幕府。

translations.literal: Jingxiu passed the jinshi and also passed the Hongci examination; recruited to the Xuanzhou prefectural staff.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxiu passed the jinshi and Hongci examinations and was recruited to the Xuanzhou prefectural staff.

sentences.zh: 入拜右補闕、起居舍人，建言：「天子視朝，宰相群臣以次對，言可傳後者，承旨宰相示左右起居，則載錄，季送史官，如故事。」

translations.literal: Entering office as Right Supplements Clerk and Recorder of the Emperor's Movements, he proposed: "When the Son of Heaven holds court, the chief minister and officials speak in turn; words worth transmitting to posterity the drafting chief minister shows the recorders of imperial movements, who enter them in the record, and each season send them to the historiographers, as custom prescribes.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as right supplements clerk and recorder of the emperor's movements and proposed that when the Son of Heaven held court and officials spoke in turn, words worth transmitting to posterity should be shown to the recorders, entered in the record, and each season sent to the historiographers as custom prescribed.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 既而執政以幾密有不可露，罷之。

translations.literal: Soon the executors of government held that some matters were too secret to disclose and abolished the practice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the executors of government held that some matters were too secret to disclose and abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 文宗將立魯王為太子，慎選師傅，敬休以戶部侍郎兼魯王傅。

translations.literal: When Wenzong was about to establish the Prince of Lu as heir apparent and carefully chose tutors, Jingxiu served as Vice Minister of Revenue concurrently as tutor to the Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong was about to establish the Prince of Lu as heir apparent and carefully chose tutors, Jingxiu served as vice minister of revenue concurrently as tutor to the Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 初，劍南西川、山南道歲征茶，戶部自遣巡院主之，募賈人入錢京師。

translations.literal: Originally Western Sichuan and the Shannan circuit levied tea tax each year; the Ministry of Revenue itself sent touring commissioners to oversee it and recruited merchants to pay money into the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Western Sichuan and the Shannan circuit levied tea tax each year; the Ministry of Revenue sent touring commissioners to oversee it and recruited merchants to pay money into the capital.

sentences.zh: 太和初，崔元略奏責本道主當歲以四萬緡上度支。

translations.literal: In early Taihe, Cui Yuanlue memorialized that the circuit itself should deliver forty thousand strings annually to the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In early Taihe Cui Yuanlue memorialized that the circuit itself should deliver forty thousand strings annually to the treasury.

sentences.zh: 久之，逗留多不至。

translations.literal: After a long time many deliveries were detained and did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time many deliveries were detained and did not arrive.

sentences.zh: 敬休始請置院秭歸，收度支錢，乃無逋沒。

translations.literal: Jingxiu first proposed establishing a bureau at Zigui to collect treasury funds, and then there were no shortfalls.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxiu first proposed establishing a bureau at Zigui to collect treasury funds, and then there were no shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 又言：「蜀道米價騰踴，百姓流亡，請以本道闕官職田賑貧民。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Along the Shu road grain prices soared; the people were displaced; I request using vacant official fields in this circuit to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that along the Shu road grain prices soared, the people were displaced, and he requested using vacant official fields in the circuit to relieve the poor.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 再為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He again served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 敬休夷淡，多容可，不飲酒食肉，不邇聲色。

translations.literal: Jingxiu was mild and detached, very accommodating, drank no wine and ate no meat, and did not approach music and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxiu was mild and detached, very accommodating, drank no wine and ate no meat, and did not approach music and beauty.

sentences.zh: 弟簡休，亦至工部侍郎。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jianxiu also rose to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jianxiu also rose to vice minister of works.
